  Every luxury manufacturer is in a relentless pursuit downmarket. There are a few reasons for this but the most important are increasing volume, amortizing common development costs and snagging life-long brand loyalists as early as possible. The Mercedes GLA is the latest entry in a growing segment: small luxury crossovers.

  Power in all models is routed to the ground via essentially the same seven-speed, dual-clutch, robotically shifted manual that we see in the Mercedes CLA. An all-wheel drive system is optional on the GLA 250 and standard on GLA 45 AMG models. The AWD system in the GLA 250 is quite similar to every other AWD in this segment using a multi-plate clutch pack to send up to 50 percent of engine power to the rear without front axle slip. Thanks to the primarily front wheel drive nature, a light curb weight of 3,428 pounds and the efficient dual clutch transmission, the GLA is easily the most efficient crossover in this category topping out at 35 mpg highway and 29 combined in the front-wheel drive model and a still impressive 25 combined in the 355 horsepower GLA 45 AMG AWD.

  Mercedes’ seven-speed DCT seems to have received a significant software update since I last sampled it in a 2014 CLA. In the sedan, the transmission hunted for gears frequently, starts were unexpectedly harsh and moderate-throttle downshifts were downright rough. The GLA 250, however, felt much like VW’s latest DSG designs:  almost as smooth as an automatic.

ceramic.snippet:
At just over 4.5-metre long, the Cupra Terramar is in the heartland family SUV class, and faces a horde of rivals. Hybrid and plug-in hybrid alternatives obviously include the Tiguan and Q3, but there's also the Toyota Rav4, Mercedes GLA, Kia Sportage, MG HS, Nissan Qashqai and Hyundai Tucson, to name a few others. That's before we've even considered pure-electric alternatives including the Tesla Model Y, BMW iX3 Neue Klasse , Audi Q4 e-tron, VW ID.4 , Skoda Enyaq, Kia EV5 and more. There are a lot of choices in this class, so the Terramar needs to be good! 

 The e-Hybrid pairs a 1.5-litre petrol turbocharged engine with an electric motor, delivering either 204hp or 272hp, depending on version. I've only driven the lower-powered Cupra Terramar e-Hybrid 204hp (in V2 trim and on 19-inch alloys wheel), but I've tried the higher-powered PHEV powertrain in the Audi Q3 , and I'd definitely say that this 204hp version is more than enough. With charge in the battery, the Terramar is smooth, quiet and responsive. Pulling away on electric power makes town driving relaxed, and there’s enough punch for confident overtakes when the petrol engine joins in. The most powerful version hits 0–62mph in around 7.

  Where the Terramar PHEV really shines is in its running costs, especially for company-car drivers. With CO₂ emissions as low as 36g/km, the Terramar e-Hybrid attracts very low Benefit-in-Kind (BIK), making it dramatically cheaper than self-charging hybrid, petrol or diesel alternatives as a company car. Pure electric cars are still much cheaper as a company car, though, and attract better tax benefits to the companies that run them, so do your maths carefully and think about whether you could live with an EV instead of a PHEV , as it'll likely save you a lot of money - despite the forthcoming 2028 eVED pay-per-mile tax. ​

# Driven: 2028 Mercedes-Benz GLA EV Is Both Familiar and a First
The electric Benz hatchback shares much with its CLA EV sibling.
At the debut of the redesigned Mercedes-Benz GLA, company chairman Ola Källenius said, “The ICE [internal-combustion engine] world and the BEV [battery-electric vehicle] world have come together.” And that’s true: Apart from their grilles, [the gas-engine GLA](https://www.caranddriver.com/mercedes-benz/gla-class-2028) and the first-ever [GLA EV](https://www.caranddriver.com/mercedes-benz/gla-class-ev) are virtually indistinguishable from each other. Källenius described the design of the new GLA as “clearly electric-first,” so it’s perhaps appropriate that the EV version is the first one we’re driving.
Electric-first is also the go-to-market strategy—at least in Europe. It was to be in the U.S., too, but there’s been a reversal; we’re now slated to get the GLA hybrid first. Really, though, we won’t be getting either one for a while. We’re told to expect the gas-engine GLA sometime late next year, while the EV won’t arrive until the first half of 2028. Our recent drive of the electric GLA in Spain, therefore, was an extra-long-lead preview.

linkup.snippet:
The GLA is supposed to be a subcompact, but the new fully electric and gas-hybrid models feel huge for the segment, and that's by design.
While in Finland for the first drive of the [2027 C-Class](https://www.jalopnik.com/2224565/2027-mercedes-benz-c-class-ev-electric-sedan-first-drive-review/), the company gave us journalists a sneak peak at the third-gen 2028 GLA ahead of its debut in Poland onWednesday, though sadly we did not get a chance to get behind the wheel.
## Your choice of EV or hybrid power  
We don't have any U.S.-spec details yet, but the electric GLA will launch in rear-wheel-drive GLA250+ and all-wheel-drive GLA350 4Matic guises. The GLA250 has 268 horsepower while the dual-motor GLA350 gets 349 horses, which will send it to 60 mph in 5.3 seconds, and the rear motors of both models have a two-speed transmission.Every electric GLA has an 800-volt architecture with an 85-kWh nickel-manganese-cobalt battery pack, which offers a range of 408 miles on the European WLTP cycle.
It can be fast-charged at up to 320 kW, adding back 168 miles in ten minutes.
The electric versions of the GLA wear the same smoked glass–effect mesh grille introduced on the [GLC EV last year](https://www.jalopnik.com/2016436/2027-mercedes-benz-glc-ev-sand-dune-drifting-first-drive-review/),with the option of 158 micro-LED lights that can create a light show for actions such as charging or when someone with a key approaches. Meanwhile, the hybrid (shown above and below) has a similar grille to the new GLB with which it also shares its platform and powertrain, with a bunch of three-pointed stars and more inletsto let its turbocharged engine breath.
The electric version on display for journalists was fitted with — stop me if you've heard this one before — the blackout Night Package and satin black paint.

octen.snippet:
2028 Mercedes-Benz GLA EV Is A Mixed Bag
Driving a 2028 Mercedes-Benz GLA won't make your nostalgic radio station jam session sound sweeter, though the 16-speaker Burmester surround sound system is very good. Collective Soul, your friend of nearly 14 years and yourself won't harmonize any better. What the third-generation GLA will do, however, is provide a frictionless, airy and easy vessel for making memories in the sun. Turn up the volume using the haptic volume knob, turn on your fixed glass panoramic roof, and heaven, let your light shine down.
Mercedes had a few journalists out to Spain to drive the 2028 GLA250+ and GLA350 in their pure EV forms. Taking a ride up the Spanish coast in a car with a glass roof is a pretty fantastic way to spend a day. I only wished I was driving a convertible along the brilliant Spanish coast once (OK, maybe twice) during the whole drive thanks to a wide open airy cabin and whisper-quiet interior. This is a workhorse of an EV, not a pleasure cruiser, and when we got down to brass tacks it was clear there is still some work to be done.
Full disclosure: Mercedes-Benz paid for me to fly to Spain, set me loose on the Spanish countryside in two fully charged GLAs, kept me fed and put me up in a hotel for two nights.
The RWD one is a genuine hoot

Before you say it, trust us—we had the same thought about the 2028 Mercedes GLA Electric. Why pick the new GLA when the Rivian R2, our 2027 SUV of the Year, is available in the same low $50,000 price range? The more we experienced the GLA, the more we understood Mercedes' EV strategy and how it's something Rivian can't compete with. Yet.
Like the new GLC electric, the GLA also attempts to wow with tech, but no matter how many displays we gazed upon or futuristic sounds we heard, passion wasn't at the top of our notes. For a specific type of buyer, the GLA may still be the right choice. Here's why.

What makes the 2028 GLA Electric a big deal is how the small SUV fills in the Mercedes EV lineup. We like the larger GLC Electric but that model's prices rise quickly with desirable options. Thanks to the 2028 GLA's expected base pricing around $50,000, Mercedes can reach more buyers.
Attention, Tesla Model Y drivers seeking mainstream luxury: Your Mercedes has arrived.
The 2028 GLA can't compete with the Model Y on interior or cargo space, but the reputation of the three-pointed star comes standard. You want status with your luxury EV? Mercedes has been building dreams on wheels for well over a century.

2028 Mercedes-Benz GLA Goes Hybrid and Electric

Redesigned luxury SUV ratchets up space, tech, and efficiency to compete with models from Audi, BMW, and Lexus

Overview

The Mercedes-Benz GLA small SUV is redesigned for the 2028 model year, drawing clear design inspiration and technical features from the automaker’s premium lineup, while growing incrementally in size to provide more passenger and cargo room.
It will be available in two electric and two hybrid configurations. There is no gas-only model.
Although it is technically an “entry-level” luxury vehicle, the GLA can be had with a wide range of high-tech features befitting top Mercedes-Benz models, such as dash-spanning screens, AI-enabled virtual assistance, Burmester audio with 3D sound, and a suite of active safety equipment. Consequently, the price range is likely to be broad, especially when indulging in optional packages.

The model range starts with the front-drive GLA 220 hybrid, and for now, tops out with the GLA 350 4MATIC Electric, with 349 hp and an 800-volt architecture.
Both the electric and hybrid GLA are scheduled to arrive at U.S. dealerships in the second half of 2027.
It competes with the Audi Q3 and Q4 E-Tron; BMW iX3 and X2; Genesis GV60, GV70, and Electrified GV70; Lexus RZ and NX Hybrid; and Volvo XC40
The powertrains are:
* 268-hp, single electric motor; 85-kWh battery; front-wheel drive
* 349-hp, dual electric motors; 85-kWh battery; all-wheel drive
* 208-hp, 1.5-liter turbocharged 4-cylinder hybrid engine; 8-speed dual-clutch automatic

seltz.snippet:
Mercedes-Benz is taking its entry-level SUV into a new era with the redesigned 2028 GLA, and the biggest change is how it will launch. Following the same playbook as the new CLA, the next GLA will arrive first as a fully electric model before hybrid versions follow. That makes the GLA one of the clearest signs yet that Mercedes is no longer treating EVs as separate specialty products, but as core versions of familiar nameplates.

The electric lineup will include the rear-wheel-drive GLA250+ and the all-wheel-drive GLA350. Mercedes has not released official horsepower figures yet, but if the closely related CLA is any indication, output could land near 268 horsepower for the GLA250+ and around 349 horsepower for the GLA350. Mercedes says the GLA350 should reach 60 mph in 5.3 seconds, while the GLA250+ is expected to be the range-focused version with an estimated driving range of about 350 miles.

Both electric versions ride on Mercedes’ new MMA platform and use an 85-kWh battery with 800-volt electrical architecture. That is important because it allows DC fast charging at up to 320 kW when connected to a powerful enough charger. For daily use and road trips, that kind of charging speed could make the electric GLA far more convenient than earlier compact luxury EVs, especially for buyers who want something premium without jumping into a larger and more expensive SUV.

Hybrid models will follow for buyers who are not ready to go fully electric. The GLA220 will use front-wheel drive, while the GLA250 will offer all-wheel drive. Like the CLA hybrid, these models are expected to pair a turbocharged 1.5-liter engine with an eight-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission. Mercedes has not announced output or fuel economy figures yet, but the strategy gives shoppers a choice between full EV driving and a more traditional hybrid setup in the same redesigned GLA family.

The new GLA also grows in size.

ultimate.snippet:
This 2028 GLA-Class Electric is set to launch in the second half of 2027 with two trims to choose from. The entry is the GLA 250+ Electric, with a single motor making 268 hp and 247 lb-ft of torque, and driving the rear wheels. When AWD isn’t needed, the front motor decouples to help increase range.

In Canadian testing, most CLA- and GLB-Class Electric models rate between 502 and 528 km on a charge, so expect this crossover to line up similarly. The charging architecture is 800 volts, and the GLA-Class is capable of fast-charging speeds as fast as 320 kW.  ... There’s also a 107-L frunk under the hood; and if you still need to take more with you, the GLA-Class can tow 2,000 kg (4,400 lb).

An available “Superscreen” stretches across the dash and incorporates the 10.25-inch instrument display, 14-inch touchscreen, and new 14-inch touchscreen for the passenger, all under a single piece of glass. If you don’t order that last screen, the other two remain but your front-seat companion gets a plain dash panel. The floating console includes cup holders and phone storage, but oddly at this premium level, it’s an option for that latter bin to include a wireless charger. ... The GLA 250+ Electric is a very good daily driver that happens to be electric. As electric vehicles do, the GLA-Class has regenerative braking, which captures otherwise-lost energy during braking and feeds it back into the battery. It can be set to four levels of none, normal, “intelligent” variable, or heavy; and in that last one, it can bring the vehicle to a complete stop without touching the brake pedal (the intelligent setting will, too, but only if there’s a vehicle stopped in front of you).

The extra power makes short work of highway passing, while it’s still easy to modulate and without any fuss in busy city driving.
